questions.question: What does the detector return for a prompt?
options: A boolean block decision only
The model's full system prompt
A list of every rule in the rulebase
A category and a confidence in [0, 1]

questions.question: Why does normalize run before substring and regex rules?
options: Because regex is slower than substring
Because the standard library forbids running rules on the original text
Because normalize lowers the file size on disk
Because normalize exposes hidden tokens such as base64, rot13, and zero-width insertions to the downstream rules

Why is the benign prompt corpus part of the evaluation?
options: To compute recall on attacks
To inflate the accuracy number
To pre-train the rules
To measure false-positive rate on safe text and catch over-broad rules

questions.question: What does the analyze method do when no rule fires?
options: Returns the category of the most recent rule attempted
Returns a random category
Returns the category benign with confidence 0.0
Raises an exception

questions.question: Why does this lesson argue the detector is not the safety gate?
options: Because the detector is implemented in Python
Because the rules are stored as data
Because the detector is too fast to be useful
Because the detector is one signal among several the gate will compose, with each signal trading precision against recall differently
